scoring_formula: domain_score = sum(question_score * question_weight) / max_possible * 100  where max_possible = sum(4 * question_weight)

tiers.free: Shown in free ReadyScore assessment. 2 highest-signal questions per domain (10 total).
tiers.paid: Shown only in full paid audit along with all free-tier questions.

domains.name: Data Security & Compliance Posture
domains.description: How well your Microsoft 365 / Entra ID tenant and data-protection program are prepared to safely enable Copilot and other AI tools without leaking regulated or confidential information.

questions.text: Which Microsoft 365 license tier covers the majority of your employees today?
questions.help_text: Your M365 license determines which security and AI features are available. Copilot for Microsoft 365 requires a qualifying base license (Business Standard / Premium / E3 / E5) plus a Copilot add-on, and many data-protection features we'll ask about below are only unlocked at Business Premium or E5.

options.label: No Microsoft 365 / we use Google Workspace or other

questions.text: Who in your organization is required to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) to sign in?
questions.help_text: MFA means signing in with a password plus a second factor (phone app, text code, hardware key). It's the single most effective control against account takeover and is a prerequisite before turning on Copilot or any AI that reads company data.

options.label: No one / MFA is not enforced
Only a few admins use it voluntarily
All admin accounts are required to use MFA
All users are required to use MFA
All users on MFA plus phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2 / Authenticator number matching)

questions.text: How are Microsoft Purview Sensitivity Labels deployed in your tenant?
questions.help_text: Sensitivity Labels are tags (e.g. Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential) you apply to files, emails, and Teams sites. They drive encryption, watermarks, and control whether Copilot can use a document. Without labels, Copilot surfaces whatever a user can open — including data they probably shouldn't be reusing.

options.label: Labels exist but users rarely apply them
Manual labeling in use, training delivered
Auto-labeling rules applied to SharePoint / OneDrive / Exchange
Auto-labeling + encryption + DLP integration across all locations

questions.text: How much coverage do your Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies have?
questions.help_text: DLP policies automatically detect and block sensitive data (SSNs, payment cards, PHI, policy numbers) from being emailed, shared externally, or uploaded to unmanaged apps. Essential for HIPAA, state bar confidentiality rules, and keeping regulated data out of public AI tools.

options.label: Default/template policies enabled in audit mode only
Policies covering email + OneDrive/SharePoint, some in enforce mode
Full coverage incl. Teams + endpoints, enforcement on
Adaptive DLP tuned with industry-specific classifiers and regular policy review

questions.text: How is your sensitive data classified and inventoried today?
questions.help_text: Before AI can safely summarize your data you need to know where the regulated stuff lives. Purview Information Protection and Data Map scan SharePoint, OneDrive, file shares, and databases to identify PHI, PII, financial data, and privileged matter files.

options.label: No classification — we don't know what we have or where
Some scanning via Purview or a third-party tool
Purview Information Protection deployed across all cloud locations
Automated classification + data-map dashboards reviewed quarterly

questions.text: Which Microsoft Defender products do you have deployed?
questions.help_text: Defender for Office 365 protects email from phishing. Defender for Cloud Apps gives visibility into shadow IT (which unsanctioned SaaS and AI tools employees are using). Defender for Endpoint protects laptops. These are what stop employees from pasting client data into random AI websites.

questions.text: How mature are your Conditional Access policies in Entra ID?
questions.help_text: Conditional Access is the traffic cop for sign-ins — it enforces rules like 'require MFA from unknown locations', 'block legacy auth', or 'only managed devices can reach SharePoint'. Required for a Zero Trust posture before turning on Copilot.

options.label: Block legacy auth + MFA for all users
Device compliance and risk-based policies in place
Zero Trust model — identity + device + app + session controls

questions.text: How are external sharing and guest access controlled in SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams?
questions.help_text: Default M365 tenants often allow 'anyone with the link' sharing. For regulated industries this is a breach waiting to happen, and Copilot will happily summarize whatever guests can see.

options.label: Guest access restricted, sharing limited to specific domains
Guest lifecycle managed, access reviews run periodically
Fully governed — entitlement management + access reviews + expiration

questions.text: What is your audit log and eDiscovery retention posture?
questions.help_text: Audit logs tell you who accessed what, when, and from where. State bar rules, HIPAA, and many contracts require you to reproduce that history months or years later. Standard M365 retains only 90–180 days; Premium/E5 extend this to a year or more.

options.label: Long-term retention + eDiscovery Premium in use
SIEM export + 7-year retention for regulated data

questions.text: Which regulatory or contractual requirements apply to your business?
questions.help_text: These frameworks dictate what data you must protect and how. Knowing which apply shapes whether Copilot, Azure OpenAI with your own tenant, or an on-prem solution is the right fit.

options.label: State insurance regulations / NAIC data standards
Oil & gas data sovereignty / operator MSA confidentiality

questions.text: Where does your business-critical data live today?
questions.help_text: Data residency affects which AI services you can legally use. Copilot processes data in the same Microsoft region as your tenant; an on-prem-only posture will require different AI architectures (local models, private endpoints).

options.label: Mostly on-prem with some cloud email

questions.text: Do you have signed Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) or Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with your key vendors?
questions.help_text: Any SaaS or AI tool that touches regulated data needs a signed BAA (HIPAA) or DPA. If you're on ChatGPT free, Grammarly free, or any consumer AI tool, regulated data shouldn't be going into it.

options.label: Some — for obvious vendors like M365

domains.name: Operational Process Maturity
domains.description: How documented and structured your day-to-day workflows are — the lower-friction those processes are, the more of them AI can automate.

questions.text: Which repetitive processes eat up the most staff time each week? Select all that apply.
questions.help_text: These are the highest-value AI automation targets. We'll use this to shape the ROI calculator downstream.

questions.text: Roughly how many documents (intake forms, quotes, claims, contracts, reports) does your team produce or process each week?
questions.help_text: High document volume is the #1 predictor of AI payback — each repeated document template is a place Copilot or a custom GPT can save hours.

questions.text: About how many emails does a typical front-office or admin staffer handle per week?
questions.help_text: Email triage, drafting, and follow-up is a classic Copilot for Outlook win.

questions.text: How is management reporting assembled today?
questions.help_text: Manual, copy-paste reporting from multiple systems is a prime target for AI + Power BI / Fabric.

options.label: Manually built in Excel each time
Mostly manual with a few saved templates

questions.text: How well documented are your core business processes?
questions.help_text: AI can only automate what a human can explain. Documented SOPs translate directly into prompts, agents, and Power Automate flows.

options.label: Nothing written down — lives in people's heads
A few critical SOPs exist, most do not
Most processes documented and reviewed yearly
SOPs versioned, tested, and continuously improved

questions.text: Roughly how many separate SaaS applications does your team use daily?
questions.help_text: Excess tool sprawl fragments your data and makes AI integration harder; consolidation is often a prerequisite step.

questions.text: When work hands off between people or departments, how reliable is the handoff?
questions.help_text: Messy handoffs waste rework time that AI agents can't fix — they compound.

options.label: Frequent drops, rework, and missed items
Works ok but requires chasing people
Clear queues / checklists / systems drive handoffs
Automated workflow with status visibility end-to-end

questions.text: How much of your inbound information arrives in digital, structured form?
questions.help_text: Paper forms, faxes, and scans require OCR before AI can read them. Digital intake shortens time-to-value.

options.label: Mostly paper, faxes, and phone calls

questions.text: Do you measure quality, turnaround, or error rates for your key processes?
questions.help_text: If you can't measure today's baseline you can't prove AI ROI tomorrow.

questions.text: About what share of work has to be redone because of errors, missing info, or compliance callbacks?
questions.help_text: High rework means AI can drive immediate quality wins — but it also means the underlying process needs structure first.

domains.name: Technology Infrastructure Readiness
domains.description: The state of the tech stack that AI will sit on top of — productivity suite, line-of-business systems, networks, and endpoints.

questions.text: What is your primary productivity and email platform?
questions.help_text: Copilot for Microsoft 365 requires an M365 tenant. Google Workspace shops should look at Gemini for Workspace instead. Mixed environments need a clearer strategy before buying AI licenses.

options.label: Mixed — some M365, some Google, some desktop Office
On-prem Exchange or legacy desktop Office only

questions.text: What is your primary line-of-business (LOB) system?
questions.help_text: The LOB system (practice management, claims system, case management, ERP) is where most automation ROI lives. Cloud-hosted LOB with APIs unlocks far more than on-prem legacy software.

options.label: No dedicated LOB — we run on Excel / Sheets
Modern cloud LOB with documented API
API-first platform with active integrations already running

questions.text: Which integration / automation platforms do you actively use?
questions.help_text: Power Automate, Zapier, or Make are the glue that turns AI outputs into real workflow changes. Existing adoption = much faster time-to-value.

options.label: Native integrations inside our LOB only

questions.text: What on-premise server infrastructure do you still maintain?
questions.help_text: Heavy on-prem footprint slows AI adoption — cloud-first tenants connect to Copilot, Azure OpenAI, and Microsoft Graph much faster.

options.label: Significant on-prem — domain controller, file server, app servers
One or two servers (e.g. file share)

questions.text: How is your network and remote-work posture?
questions.help_text: AI tools and Copilot need reliable bandwidth and modern identity. Legacy VPNs that break when users work remotely also break AI adoption.

options.label: Adequate bandwidth, traditional VPN for remote
Modern SSO + cloud apps accessible from anywhere
Zero Trust network access with device posture checks

questions.text: How are employee laptops and phones managed?
questions.help_text: Microsoft Intune (or equivalent MDM) is how you enforce that only compliant, encrypted, patched devices access company data and AI tools. Without it, Copilot can still be used — but the regulated data it touches may flow to untrusted devices.

options.label: Not managed — users own their devices and configuration
Basic anti-virus on company-issued laptops only
Intune or similar MDM deployed, partial coverage
Full Intune deployment — compliance policies + app protection
Autopilot + compliance + conditional access fully integrated

questions.text: What is your backup and disaster recovery posture?
questions.help_text: AI doesn't cause data loss but amplifies dependence on the data. A ransomware event that takes out SharePoint takes Copilot with it.

options.label: Cloud backup with periodic restore testing
3-2-1 with documented RPO/RTO and quarterly test restores

questions.text: What is your primary identity provider for signing in to apps?
questions.help_text: Copilot and most modern AI assistants use Entra ID (Azure AD) identity for permissions and audit. Fragmented identity = fragmented AI governance.

options.label: Per-app local accounts, no central identity
Entra ID (Azure AD) for M365 plus some SSO
Entra ID with SSO to most business apps
Google Workspace identity for most apps

questions.text: Do you have a central data warehouse, lakehouse, or analytics platform?
questions.help_text: Not required for many AI wins (Copilot works on docs + email directly), but necessary for predictive/analytical AI use cases.

options.label: No — data lives in source systems only
Power BI / Looker with curated datasets
Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, or similar modern lakehouse

questions.text: Do you know what AI tools your employees are already using personally for work?
questions.help_text: Shadow AI (ChatGPT free, Claude.ai, consumer Copilot, Grammarly, etc.) is the biggest silent data-leak vector today. Visibility is step one.

options.label: No idea — we don't monitor it
Defender for Cloud Apps / discovery tool in place
Sanctioned-AI list enforced, shadow AI blocked or redirected

domains.name: Team & Change Management
domains.description: The people side: who owns technology internally, how your workforce reacts to change, and whether leadership will champion AI adoption.

questions.text: Who owns technology decisions day-to-day in your business?
questions.help_text: AI programs fail without a clear decision-maker. An MSP can be enough, but someone inside the business needs authority to prioritize.

options.label: No one specific — owner / partners handle it ad-hoc
An outside MSP, no internal champion
Office manager / ops lead handles it alongside other duties
Internal IT lead or MSP + internal champion
Dedicated IT / digital leader with budget authority

questions.text: How would you describe leadership's current stance on AI adoption?
questions.help_text: Executive sponsorship is the single biggest success factor. Cautious is fine; blocked is a red flag.

options.label: Blocked — leadership has banned AI tools
Skeptical — concerned about risk and cost
Cautious but open to structured pilots
Champion — has set explicit AI strategy and budget

questions.text: How comfortable is your staff with new technology generally?
questions.help_text: Pilot success depends on user adoption. Mixed comfort is normal — we design the rollout accordingly.

options.label: Very resistant — adoption is always a struggle
Slow to adopt, needs heavy hand-holding
Generally eager to try new tools

questions.text: How have prior technology rollouts gone at your business?
questions.help_text: Past is prologue. Consistent failures usually reflect process, not people — we'll account for that in the plan.

options.label: Have never rolled out anything major
Rollouts routinely stall or roll back

questions.text: How is staff training handled today?
questions.help_text: Copilot adoption without training yields 20–30% of the possible ROI. Structured enablement is non-negotiable.

options.label: Continuous learning culture with dedicated budget

questions.text: Do you have a written acceptable-use policy for AI tools?
questions.help_text: A one-page AI use policy (what data can go in, what tools are approved, what's banned) is table-stakes before any pilot.

options.label: Draft policy exists, not yet rolled out
Published policy and staff have acknowledged it
Policy, training, and enforcement via DLP / Purview

questions.text: Are there any organized groups or constraints that will slow rollout?
questions.help_text: Unionized, regulated, or heavily credentialed workforces aren't blockers — they just need different playbooks.

options.label: Licensed / regulated professionals (MDs, attorneys, CPAs, PEs)

questions.text: Is there a power user or internal champion excited to pilot AI?
questions.help_text: One motivated champion per department is worth more than any vendor trainer.

domains.name: Financial & Strategic Alignment
domains.description: Whether budget, decision-making speed, and strategic priorities line up with realistic AI timelines and ROI.

questions.text: What is your approximate annual revenue?
questions.help_text: Used to right-size recommendations. We don't share this outside the report.

questions.text: What is your realistic timeline for making a meaningful AI investment?
questions.help_text: This sets the cadence — a 90-day pilot looks very different from a 2-year roadmap.

questions.text: What is your approximate annual technology budget (software + IT services)?
questions.help_text: Tech budget as a share of revenue is the cleanest indicator of capacity to act.

questions.text: How are technology purchase decisions usually made?
questions.help_text: Single owners move in weeks; boards move in quarters. Neither is wrong — it just shapes the engagement.

options.label: Single owner decides — can move in days

questions.text: Which strategic priorities matter most in the next 12 months? Select up to 3.
questions.help_text: Different drivers point to different AI use cases. Cost reduction → back-office automation; growth → sales/marketing AI; compliance → Purview + governance.

options.label: Keep up with competitors already using AI

questions.text: Have you invested in AI or automation tools before?
questions.help_text: Past experiments — good or bad — tell us where to start and what to avoid.

options.label: Have at least one AI tool in daily use
Multiple AI tools in production, measurable ROI

questions.text: What ROI expectation are you bringing to this project?
questions.help_text: Realistic expectations are a leading indicator of success. AI pilots for SMBs in these industries typically return 2–5x in year one when done well.

options.label: Cost savings of a specific headcount or $ amount

questions.text: Are you willing to measure a baseline before the pilot starts?
questions.help_text: 2 weeks of pre-pilot time-tracking is the cheapest insurance policy for proving ROI later.

options.label: No — not willing to slow down for that
Yes — we already track some of these metrics
Absolutely — we want clear before/after data
